title: YOU CANNOT BUY AWAY A WRONG

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But Hamor said to them, 'My son Shechem has his heart set on your daughter. Please give her to him as his wife. Intermarry with us; give us your daughters and take our daughters for yourselves. You can settle among us; the land is open to you. Live in it, trade in it, and acquire property in it.' Then Shechem said to Dinah's father and brothers, 'Let me find favor in your eyes, and I will give you whatever you ask. Make the price for the bride and the gift I am to bring as great as you like, and I'll pay whatever you ask me. Only give me the young woman as my wife.'" - Gen 34:8-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Hamor and Shechem come with a proposal, and it is striking for what it leaves out. Not once do they say, "We are sorry." There is no acknowledgment of the terrible wrong done to Dinah, no repentance, no shame. Instead, they treat the whole matter as a business deal: name your price, marry into our families, settle here, trade, prosper. Shechem even offers, "I will give you whatever you ask."

This is a picture of trying to smooth over a grievous wrong without ever facing it. Hamor and Shechem hoped that generous terms and future benefits would make the offence disappear. But a wound like Dinah's cannot simply be paid off. Money and marriage cannot undo the injustice or heal the pain.

We can fall into a version of this ourselves. When we have hurt someone, we may be tempted to move quickly past it — to offer a gift, a favour, a quick "let's just move on" — without ever truly acknowledging the wrong or repenting of it. But real reconciliation begins with honest confession, not a smooth transaction.

If you have wronged someone, do not try to buy your way past it. Own it. Name it. Ask forgiveness humbly. God Himself calls us to genuine repentance, not cover-ups (Prov 28:13). Grace flows where wrongs are honestly faced, not where they are hurriedly bought off.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I ever tempted to "buy away" a wrong instead of facing it?
2. Does true reconciliation in my life begin with honest confession?
3. Where do I need to name and own a wrong rather than smooth it over?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from trying to cover over my wrongs with gifts or excuses. Give me the honesty to confess, the humility to repent, and the courage to make things right. Amen.
